{{Short description|Russian physicist (born 1944)}}
'''Boris Ionovich Shklovskii''' (born 1944) is a Russian theoretical [[physicist]], at the [[William I Fine Theoretical Physics Institute, University of Minnesota]], specializing in [[condensed matter]]. Shklovskii earned his A.B. degree in [[Physics]], in 1966 and a Ph.D. in [[condensed matter]] theory, in 1968 from [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad University]].<ref name=umnbio>[https://www.physics.umn.edu/people/shklovsk.html UMN BIO physics Shklovskii] Retrieved 28 April 2019.</ref>

Shklovskii is known for the [[Variable-range hopping#Efros–Shklovskii variable-range hopping|Efros–Shklovskii variable-range hopping conductivity]], a model for the temperature dependence of the electrical conductivity in the variable-range hopping regime.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Efros, A.L.|author2=Van Lien, Nguyen|author3=Shklovskii, B.I.|year=1979|title=Variable range hopping in doped crystalline semiconductors|journal=Solid State Communications|volume=32|issue=10|pages=851–854|doi=10.1016/0038-1098(79)90484-8|bibcode=1979SSCom..32..851E|issn=0038-1098}}</ref>
He has also made important contributions to the theory of the [[Quantum Hall effect]] (explaining the structure of conducting edge channels<ref name="Chklovskii Shklovskii Glazman 1992 pp. 4026–4034">{{cite journal | last1=Chklovskii | first1=D. B. | last2=Shklovskii | first2=B. I. | last3=Glazman | first3=L. I. |author3-link=Leonid Glazman | title=Electrostatics of edge channels | journal=Physical Review B | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=46 | issue=7 | date=1992-08-15 | issn=0163-1829 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.46.4026 | pages=4026–4034| pmid=10004131 | bibcode=1992PhRvB..46.4026C }}</ref> and predicting the formation of Quantum Hall stripe and bubble phases<ref name="Koulakov Fogler Shklovskii 1996 pp. 499–502">{{cite journal | last1=Koulakov | first1=A. A. | last2=Fogler | first2=M. M. | last3=Shklovskii | first3=B. I. | title=Charge Density Wave in Two-Dimensional Electron Liquid in Weak Magnetic Field | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=76 | issue=3 | date=1996-01-15 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.76.499 | pages=499–502| pmid=10061472 | arxiv=cond-mat/9508017 | bibcode=1996PhRvL..76..499K | s2cid=41126815 }}</ref><ref name="Fogler Koulakov Shklovskii 1996 pp. 1853–1871">{{cite journal | last1=Fogler | first1=M. M. | last2=Koulakov | first2=A. A. | last3=Shklovskii | first3=B. I. | title=Ground state of a two-dimensional electron liquid in a weak magnetic field | journal=Physical Review B | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=54 | issue=3 | date=1996-07-15 | issn=0163-1829 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.54.1853 | pages=1853–1871| pmid=9986033 | arxiv=cond-mat/9601110 | bibcode=1996PhRvB..54.1853F | s2cid=13279439 }}</ref>) and to the theory of [[macromolecules]] (developing the theory of electrostatic charge inversion<ref name="Shklovskii 1999 pp. 5802–5811">{{cite journal | last=Shklovskii | first=B. I. | title=Screening of a macroion by multivalent ions: Correlation-induced inversion of charge | journal=Physical Review E | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=60 | issue=5 | date=1999-11-01 | issn=1063-651X | doi=10.1103/physreve.60.5802 | pages=5802–5811| pmid=11970478 | arxiv=cond-mat/9907351 | bibcode=1999PhRvE..60.5802S | s2cid=25976742 }}</ref><ref name="Grosberg Nguyen Shklovskii 2002 pp. 329–345">{{cite journal | last1=Grosberg | first1=A. Yu. | last2=Nguyen | first2=T. T. | last3=Shklovskii | first3=B. I. | title=Colloquium: The physics of charge inversion in chemical and biological systems | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=74 | issue=2 | date=2002-04-19 | issn=0034-6861 | doi=10.1103/revmodphys.74.329 | pages=329–345| bibcode=2002RvMP...74..329G }}</ref>).

==Honors and awards==
Shklovskii was awarded the Landau Prize of Academy of Sciences of USSR in 1986, the A.S. Fine Chair in Theoretical Physics in 1990,<ref name=umnbio/><ref>[https://cse.umn.edu/r/honorary-professorships/#Endowed UMN CSE Endowed Chairs and Professorship] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328092404/https://cse.umn.edu/r/honorary-professorships/#Endowed |date=2016-03-28 }} Retrieved 28 April 2019.</ref> and was elected a [[fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1997.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow archive|publisher=APS|access-date=18 June 2020}} </ref>

In 2018, he received the [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize|2019 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Physics Prize]] for "''pioneering research in the physics of disordered materials and hopping conductivity''" together with [[Alexei L. Efros]] and [[Elihu Abrahams]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Shklovskii&first_nm=Boris&year=2019|title=2019 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Physics Prize Recipient|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref>

In 2023 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cse.umn.edu/physics/news/shklovskii-elected-national-academy-sciences?last_nm=Shklovskii&first_nm=Boris&year=2023|title=Shklovskii elected to the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering|access-date=8 August 2024}}</ref>
